questions.q: What are the four courses in the Data Engineering track, in order?
options: Data Engineering Foundations, Azure Databricks & Delta Lake, Microsoft Fabric & Real-Time Analytics, Data Engineering Career & Capstone
T-SQL, Power BI, Snowflake, dbt
Foundations, Airflow, Kafka, Career & Capstone
Databricks & Delta Lake, Fabric & Real-Time Analytics, Foundations, Career & Capstone
questions.explain: This course is the fourth and final course in the track, tying together the vocabulary from Foundations, the scale-out patterns from Databricks & Delta Lake, and the real-time patterns from Fabric & Real-Time Analytics.

questions.q: What is the real point of the three capstone projects, according to this finale?
options: Proving that the earlier three courses' techniques compose into real, working systems — batch, migration, and streaming alike
Teaching entirely new material not covered anywhere else in the track
Replacing the need for the DP-700 certification prep chapter
Testing whether AI tools alone can build a data platform
questions.explain: The retail platform, warehouse migration, and fraud detector are evidence the same underlying toolkit handles genuinely different shapes of system.

questions.q: How does this finale describe AI's role across the track, honestly?
options: Genuinely useful in specific places, like drafting documentation or explaining a query, but not a replacement for the judgment behind a trade-off decision
AI replaces the need for system design thinking entirely
AI is never useful for data engineering work
AI should be used for every decision instead of human judgment
questions.explain: Chapter 3's honest treatment of AI carries into the finale — helpful as a tool, but the reasoning behind a real design decision is still the engineer's to make and defend.

questions.q: According to this lesson, which courses in the broader catalog are natural next steps for going further than this track?
options: Git/GitHub/CI-CD, Terraform/Bicep-focused material, Airflow, and Kafka
T-SQL and Power BI, as prerequisites that should have come first
There are no further courses relevant to this track
Only the DP-700 certification exam itself
questions.explain: These already exist as separate courses in the catalog and extend the deployment, infrastructure, orchestration, and streaming ideas this track introduced.

questions.q: What does this finale say a student is actually "ready" for, since there's no next lesson?
options: Being able to open any of the three capstone projects and walk someone through it, start to finish, in their own words
Immediately starting a fifth course in the track
Retaking the DP-700 practice exam from Chapter 2
Deleting the capstone projects since the course is finished
questions.explain: The finale replaces the usual 'Check yourself' question with this direct measure of readiness, since the portfolio and interview story are the actual deliverables of the whole track.
